why: The new contradiction‑veto and no‑internal‑split principles made the scorer avoid boundaries that would leave a left fragment that contradicts the whole sentence and avoid some particle/attachment cuts, and the conditional dense‑cut rule partly recovered denser short‑latency choices; this produced small gains in the short bins (≤3–≤7) but caused many cuts to be displaced into intra‑word/character positions or earlier long‑latency boundaries, producing the long‑bin degradations and the internal splits seen in the tails.
lesson: When adding contradiction vetoes or banning particle/word splits, ensure the scorer is constrained so it does not simply shift boundaries into intra‑word/character positions or earlier long‑latency cuts — enforce no‑internal‑split without creating new illegal splits and apply contradiction checks narrowly so they don't displace previously good long‑latency boundaries.
